$comment: Nightly MEL -> website sync (scripts/sync-from-mel.mjs). MEL is read-only, always. Fields are addressed by FIELD ID in both bases so a rename cannot silently break the mapping; the one exception is the override checkbox, which is looked up by NAME at run time (see website.overrideFieldsByName). The website base's Countries follow MEL's 'Places of operation'; Status, Cohort label and Undercover? are computed too but only written when listed under sync.fields.

placeTypes.$comment: Values of Places -> Type. A country is listed as itself; a subnational entity contributes its parent country (the 'Is part of' link of type country); the regions below are kept as the website option of the same name; every other region and income group is dropped.

overrideFieldsByName.$comment: Checkbox per synced field: ticked = this row is curated by hand, the sync never writes that field. Resolved from the base schema by name at run time; --apply refuses to run if a listed checkbox is missing.

overrideFieldIds.$comment: Known ids of the checkboxes above, used only as a fallback (with a warning) when no field of that name exists, i.e. someone renamed it. The name lookup wins when both resolve.

stateFieldsByName.$comment: Long-text field per synced field, OWNED BY THE SYNC: MEL's derived value as of the last run, written for every linked row (comma-separated, sorted; '(none)' when MEL has nothing). It is what lets a hand-curated row be flagged once, when MEL changes, instead of every night for as long as it differs. Resolved by name at run time; --apply refuses to run if a listed field is missing. Never edit by hand.

stateFieldIds.$comment: Known ids of the state fields above, fallback when renamed (see overrideFieldIds).

sync.$comment: fields: which computed fields are written to existing rows (keys of the registry in scripts/lib/mel-sync.mjs: countries, status, cohortLabel, undercover). Add a key here, add its override checkbox above, and the nightly job starts writing it. createMissingRows: a MEL charity with no website row gets one (Display name, MEL Charity ID, Cohort label, Status, Countries; Undercover? ticked when MEL says so; Website ready? left unticked).

countryNameMap.$comment: MEL uses UN names; the website's Countries options and data/continents.json use the common short names. Add a line here when a new UN-style name shows up (the dry run lists target names that are not yet a Countries option or not in continents.json).

cohortLabel.$comment: MEL cohort name -> website Cohort label. Trimmed (MEL has trailing spaces on some names), then each key below is replaced by its value. Convention on the website field: '2019', '2025 H1', '2024 Effective Giving'.
